references.text: God explains that no one can see His face and live, which is the background for why Moses only gets to see God's back.
The fulfillment of the promise that the Lord will pass by Moses and reveal His glory.
Elijah on Horeb experiences a similar theophany where the Lord passes by, but God is not in the wind, earthquake, or fire.
Isaiah sees the Lord's glory in the temple, but even this vision of God's throne is a limited revelation.
No one has ever seen God, but the only Son has made Him known – a New Testament reflection on the limitation of seeing God.
Jesus says that whoever has seen Him has seen the Father – in Christ, God's face is fully revealed.
God dwells in light no one can approach, and no one has seen or can see Him – confirming that God's full glory is inaccessible to humans.
Contrasting revelations: The temporary absence of the incarnate God (John) versus the permanent invisibility of the infinite God (Ex).
